REVOLUTION THEORY — LANDSCAPE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

         WHAT CAUSES REVOLUTIONS?
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  Grievances alone don't explain timing     │
         │  Ideology alone doesn't explain success    │
         │  Structure alone doesn't explain variation │
         └────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
  Three theory clusters explain revolutionary outcomes:

  STRUCTURAL THEORIES:
    Skocpol: state / class / international triangle.
    Goldstone: demographic-structural model.

  POLITICAL PROCESS THEORIES:
    Tilly: contentious repertoires, WUNC.
    McAdam: political opportunity.

  PHENOMENOLOGICAL THEORIES:
    Arendt: public freedom, new beginning, council form.

  All three try to answer: why do some revolutions succeed
  and others don't (the selection problem)?

SKOCPOL'S CAUSAL TRIANGLE
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

         INTERNATIONAL PRESSURE
         (military competition,
          fiscal demands, war)
                │
                ▼
  STATE CRISIS:
    Fiscal breakdown and administrative incapacity. The state
    cannot meet fiscal/military demands of international
    competition without extracting from landlords.

  Two coupled fault lines emerge from a state crisis:

  LANDLORD ELITE DEFECTION:
    Old elites block state reform and paralyze the center.

  PEASANT AUTONOMY:
    Strong village communities. Peasant revolt becomes possible
    when the landlord-state alliance breaks.
                │                │
                └────────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
              REVOLUTIONARY SITUATION
              (dual power: old regime
               and challenger both claim
               sovereignty)
                         │
                         ▼
              REVOLUTIONARY OUTCOME
              (depends on which
               coalition wins the
               resulting state-building
               competition)

SKOCPOL COMPARISON TABLE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
                     France 1789   Russia 1917   China 1911-49
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Pressure              competition   catastrophe   Japan invasion
                      with Britain

State Crisis          Fiscal        Military      Warlordism +
                      bankruptcy    collapse      KMT incapacity

Landlord Block        Nobility      Nobility      Gentry/KMT
                      blocked tax   blocked       blocked
                      reform        reform        reform

Peasant Autonomy      High —        Medium —      High — village
                      strong        commune       autonomy
                      village life  tradition     in interior

Outcome               Jacobin       Bolshevik     Maoist
                      centralization centralization agrarian
                      + Napoleon    + Stalin      mobilization
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

GOLDSTONE'S DEMOGRAPHIC-STRUCTURAL PRESSURES
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  POPULATION        →    FISCAL STRESS    →    STATE CRISIS
  GROWTH                 (more people to        (can't pay
                          tax, more claims       army or
                          on state)              officials)
      │
      ▼
  ELITE               →    ELITE             →    INTRA-ELITE
  COMPETITION              OVERPRODUCTION         CONFLICT
  (more aspirants          (too many             (factions
   than positions)          educated elites        fight for
                            competing for          shrinking
                            fixed posts)           pie)
      │
      ▼
  POPULAR              →    SUBSISTENCE      →    MASS
  GROWTH                    CRISIS                MOBILIZATION
                            (rising food           (peasants /
                             prices, declining      urban poor)
                             real wages)

  THREE PRESSURES CONVERGING = REVOLUTIONARY CRISIS

TILLY: REPERTOIRE OF CONTENTION
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  Pre-modern repertoire:          Modern repertoire:
  ┌─────────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ • Grain seizures    │         │ • Strikes           │
  │ • Tax rebellions    │   →     │ • Demonstrations    │
  │ • Charivari         │ (18-19c) │ • Marches          │
  │ • Patron petitions  │         │ • Electoral campaigns│
  │ • Crowd actions     │         │ • Petition drives   │
  │   (local, direct,   │         │ (national, modular, │
  │    particular)      │         │  autonomous)        │
  └─────────────────────┘         └─────────────────────┘

  Key shift: from particular, direct, local claims
             to modular, autonomous, national claims

  Modular: same action (strike, march) can be used
           by different groups for different ends

ARENDT: AMERICAN VS. FRENCH REVOLUTIONARY LOGICS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  AMERICAN REVOLUTION           FRENCH REVOLUTION
  ┌─────────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ Goal: Foundation of │       │ Goal: Liberation    │
  │ new political order │       │ from misery (social) │
  │                     │       │                     │
  │ "Public happiness"  │       │ "Compassion for the │
  │ — participation in  │       │  poor" unleashes    │
  │   public affairs    │       │  Terror             │
  │                     │       │                     │
  │ Political question: │       │ Social question     │
  │ How shall we govern │       │ overwhelms:         │
  │ ourselves?          │       │ endless suffering   │
  │                     │       │ cannot be resolved  │
  │ Constitution as     │       │ politically         │
  │ founding act        │       │                     │
  │                     │       │ Robespierre:        │
  │ Result: stable      │       │ "virtue and terror" │
  │ republic            │       │                     │
  └─────────────────────┘       └─────────────────────┘

  KEY DISTINCTION:
  Political revolution (freedom) vs.
  Social revolution (liberation from necessity)
  Arendt: only the political revolution can succeed on its own terms

COLOR REVOLUTION MODEL
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  Fraudulent election → mass popular protest
         │
         ▼
  Security forces refuse to fire (crucial)
         │
         ▼
  Elite defection from old regime
         │
         ▼
  New leadership elected

  WHY IT WORKS:
  • WUNC requirements met (peaceful, mass, legitimate)
  • International support (EU/US signal recognition)
  • Security forces don't want to be on the losing side

  WHY IT FAILS:
  • Security forces loyal (Belarus 2020, Burma 2021)
  • Old elites reconsolidate (Kyrgyzstan after 2005)
  • No institutional depth to sustain change
  • Russia destabilizes successful cases (Ukraine 2014)

REVOLUTIONARY SUCCESS CONDITIONS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  NECESSARY CONDITIONS (Skocpol-Goldstone)
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. State fiscal/military crisis         │
  │ 2. Elite defection (old guard fractures)│
  │ 3. Mass mobilization capacity           │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
               +
  SUFFICIENT CONDITIONS (Tilly + process)
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 4. Security force defection or collapse │
  │    (army won't fire = regime falls)     │
  │ 5. Challenger coalition coherent enough │
  │    to build new state apparatus         │
  │ 6. International context permissive     │
  │    (no great-power intervention to      │
  │     restore old regime)                 │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
               =
  REVOLUTIONARY OUTCOME
  (Not just situation, but transfer +
   structural change)
